Senior Outsourcing Manager

**Your impact begins here

**As Senior Outsourcing Manager, you will lead the outsourcing projects that keep Novo’s drug development moving. Working with experts across Novo and external CMO partners worldwide, you will drive strong progress and high-quality deliveries from project start to completion. You will also be part of shaping global strategic CMO collaborations, bringing new treatments closer to the people who need them. Your impact begins with every project you lead.

**What You’ll Bring

**You bring solid drug development experience and the confidence to lead across functions and organisations.

• A MSc or PhD in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Engineering or another relevant life science.

• 4–6+ years of experience from the pharmaceutical, biotechnology or another highly regulated industry.

• A strong understanding of the R&D value chain, drug development processes and Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) requirements.

• Experience with outsourcing, CMO/CDMO collaboration and ideally contract negotiations.

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, and the ability to navigate a complex, interdisciplinary organisation.

• The ability to create structure, turn information into clear presentations and build trust across functions and with external partners.

• A proactive, positive and independent way of working, and the ability to manage several tasks at once in a fast-paced environment.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

**What You’ll Do

**You will manage outsourcing projects within drug substance and chemical synthesis, and make sure Novo and its CMO partners work as one team.

• Lead outsourcing projects from initiation to completion, keeping progress strong and deliveries high in quality.

• Select and approve CMOs, and build collaborative external partnerships.

• Negotiate and maintain relevant agreements in close collaboration with Contract Managers.

• Protect Novo’s intellectual property rights while delivering high-quality assessments on time.

• Bring colleagues across Novo together, using informal leadership to influence decisions, drive progress and lead complex projects with colleagues and partners.

• You will have significant responsibility and visibility across the business unit, using your informal leadership to influence decisions, drive progress, and lead complex projects with colleagues and partners.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join the CMC Outsourcing & Business Development team in CMC Development, part of Global Manufacturing & Supply. CMC Development develops, manufactures and distributes drug candidates for non-clinical and clinical trials. The CMC Outsourcing team supports the Novo development pipeline and has around 30 experienced colleagues responsible for sourcing and outsourcing activities across CMC Development.

Based in Bagsværd, you will work with external CMO partners globally and with colleagues across Global Research, Quality, Regulatory, Chemical Development, Manufacturing Development, Purchasing and Commercial Manufacturing. Close collaboration with Contract Managers will help you move agreements forward. You will have significant responsibility and visibility across the business unit, and the clarity you create around priorities will help teams decide, act and deliver.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will be trusted to take the lead on complex projects and be visible across the business unit. The role gives you broad organisational exposure across the drug development value chain, and the chance to build new skills while working with experts inside and outside Novo.

We embrace experimentation and strive for excellence without fixating on perfection. You will have a team to contribute to, and the support to perform at your best.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600 to 1,091,600 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn strong partnerships into progress for Novo’s drug development pipeline, apply for the Senior Outsourcing Manager role by 8 November 2026.

For further information, please contact Ralf Toftgaard Dann (Associate Director) on RTD@novonordisk.com or at +45 3079 0659

Are you eager to influence the future direction of Arla Foods? Do you envision yourself as a future leader?

How will you make an impact?

The Arla F15 Graduate Programme is a two-year, international development programme designed for graduates who want to learn quickly, explore different areas of a global business and grow into future leadership opportunities.`

Through three eight-month rotations, you will work on meaningful business projects, build an international network and develop the confidence, skills and experience to make an impact at Arla. Business areas for projects may include Marketing, Sales, HR, Strategy, Sustainability, Business Development, and Supply Chain. We will match you with a suitable department based on business needs and your profile, offering you the chance to learn and make a difference. Your F15 Graduate journey begins on 1st September 2027.

• First rotation (8 months - Aarhus, Denmark) Based at one of our offices in Aarhus you will be assigned a strategically important project somewhere in the business.

• Second rotation (8 months - Outside Denmark) You will have more influence over your second project assignment, which will give you the opportunity to continue growing in a meaningful way whilst adding real value to Arla.

• Third rotation (8 months - Any Arla market) You will collaborate with the business to source potential high impact projects for your third rotation. You will have the most influence over projects during your final rotation.

What will make you a successful F15 Graduate?

To apply for the F15 Graduate Programme, please ensure that you meet the following criteria

• You should either be in the process of completing, or have completed, a bachelor’s or master’s degree between September 2025 and September 2027. We welcome diverse educational backgrounds but seek candidates with a strong drive towards a business-focused career.

• International experience gained from working, studying or volunteering abroad is an advantage.

• Preferably at least one year of relevant work experience from student jobs or a minimum of six months of internship experience.

• You are globally mobile and willing to go on one or two rotations abroad during the two-year programme. As your first rotation is based in Aarhus, Denmark you will need to relocate unless you already reside in the local area. Arla Foods will support you with this relocation.

This programme will suit graduates who have leadership aspirations and an ambitious mindset, which combines strategic thinking with a passion for results. A global mindset is essential, as is the ability to build positive relationships and strong influencing skills. The ideal candidate should be curious, competitive, and open to change, demonstrating resilience, while also being humble, self-aware, and open to feedback.

Throughout the rotations you will receive a variety of development opportunities every step of the way. To ensure your professional and personal development, you will benefit from

• Responsibilities from day one, enabling on-the-job learning in three different areas

• Graduate development camps, taking place in different markets with your graduate colleagues

• One-to-one mentoring and sparring from senior leaders

• Be part of a supportive graduate community across all Arla Futures programmes

Important information before applying

The application period for the F15 Graduate Programme runs from 2nd November 2026 until 23.59 CET on 3rd January 2027. Before applying, please ensure you have prepared your CV and cover letter in English. You will be asked a series of questions on the application page, so we recommend that you start the application process from a computer instead of a mobile phone.

For additional information, read more about the F15 Graduate Programme on our website. Here, you can get inspiration from some of our previous and current F15s and learn more about the programme. You can also read more about what to expect from the recruitment process.

As part of your graduate journey, we’ll provide you with broad and well-rounded experience across Arla’s IT & Digital organisation. Your rotations could take you into areas such as data science, solutions consultancy, network consultancy, cybersecurity, or others.

By experiencing different parts of IT & Digital, you’ll start to understand not only the technology behind a global organisation, but also the people and business needs it supports. You’ll leave the programme with broader experience, a strong network and a clearer understanding of where you want to take your career at Arla.

We’re looking for an experienced Financial Controller to take full ownership of our numbers as we scale. You’ll run a tight month-end close, get our SaaS revenue accounting airtight, and build the finance processes that let us grow fast without drowning in manual work. If you like turning messy into robust, read on.

**About Pandektes

**Legal research hasn’t changed much in decades. Lawyers still spend countless hours navigating fragmented sources, outdated systems, and complex databases just to find the information they need.

At Pandektes, we’re changing that.

Our ambition is to build the leading global platform for legal research and the largest AI-powered legal database. By combining artificial intelligence, intelligent search, and continuously updated legal sources, we’re redefining how legal knowledge is accessed, understood, analyzed, and applied.

Pandektes has raised more than _€_17.5 million and most recently closed a _€_13.5 million Series A round (October 2026) led by Alstin Capital, PROfounders and Scale Capital. Pandektes already serves more than 450 customers across Denmark, Germany and Switzerland.

We’re still early in the journey, and joining our team now means you’ll have big impact on shaping how we scale.

**About The Role

**This is a hands-on role responsible for ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial information, overseeing the month-end close, management accounts, financial reporting and statutory compliance, while continuously improving financial processes, systems and internal controls and working closely with Senior Management, external service providers and the wider business teams. The role will combine strong technical accounting expertise with a proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

**What You’ll Do

**

• Own the monthly and annual close – reviewing journals, accruals, prepayments, provisions and balance sheet reconciliations, and delivering accurate trial balances and financial statements on time

• Make sure our SaaS revenue (subscription, usage-based and implementation) is recognised correctly, and reconcile revenue schedules to billing, contracts and the general ledger

• Produce reliable monthly P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reporting

• Take over revenue billing from the sales team and run it within finance

• Manage our outsourced service providers and review the reconciliations they prepare – bank, intercompany, payroll, fixed assets and other control accounts

• Design and maintain financial policies, controls and approval limits across payments, expenses, procurement and system access

• Oversee AP, AR and cashbook accounting, manage payments through Corepay, and keep an eye on working capital

• Lead statutory accounts and external audits, and oversee VAT, corporate tax and compliance with our tax advisers

• Coordinate intercompany accounting and reporting across our entities in Denmark, Germany, Switzerland and the UK

• Improve finance processes, systems and automation – and over time, build and develop a small accounting team

**What You’ll Bring

**

• 7+ years in commercially focused accounting roles, ideally with previous experience as a Financial Controller

• A recognised Danish accounting qualification (or equivalent, e.g. ACA, ACCA or CIMA)

• Hands-on experience with subscription and deferred revenue, including month-end revenue reconciliations

• A track record of independently running the month-end close and producing accurate management accounts

• Experience with intercompany balances, foreign currencies and reporting across international subsidiaries

• Exposure to international tax, VAT and transfer pricing, and experience running a local audit process

• A strong grasp of internal controls, segregation of duties and fraud risk

• Experience improving finance operations in a growing, scaling business – and a love for systems and automation

• A sharp eye for detail and the analytical instinct to tell a real business issue from an accounting error

**How We Work

**We place great value on a vibrant, inspiring, and challenging company culture. This is achieved through a talented and passionate team that believes in achieving great things together.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We believe that ownership is what brings us the best teams – you can expect a lot of freedom and responsibility. The key is open communication, trust, and a shared passion to transform the legal world.

We are a growing team based in Copenhagen, Hamburg, London and Zurich. This role will be based in our Copenhagen HQ.

**What we offer

**

• Competitive compensation + an attractive warrant program

• A collaborative work environment where your input is not only valued but often implemented within hours

• A central office in Copenhagen, where you can work closely with an ambitious and growing team

• International team events – last time we went to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you join us next time

• 25 vacation days per year + public holidays

• Your own Pleo card for necessary work expenses

• Paid parental leave

jobs.occupation: Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027.

Research area and project description:

How can grazing management be optimized to benefit both biodiversity and nature-based beef production? This PhD project will address this question through analyses of long-term biodiversity monitoring data, development of digital biodiversity indicators, and field experiments in Danish semi-natural habitats.

Grazing is a key ecological process in many ecosystems. However, biodiversity outcomes depend on how grazing is managed, including grazing intensity and timing. Despite its widespread use as a conservation tool, important knowledge gaps remain regarding which grazing strategies deliver the greatest biodiversity benefits and how these outcomes can be documented in a robust and scalable way.

The PhD project is part of the interdisciplinary Nature&Beef initiative and will combine ecology, biodiversity monitoring, remote sensing and data science. The selected candidate will work with unique datasets from the Danish national biodiversity monitoring programme (NOVANA), field experiments, drone imagery and other digital monitoring approaches.

The project will focus on four interconnected themes:

• 
Identifying grazing practices associated with positive biodiversity outcomes using long-term monitoring data.

• 
Evaluating the effects of grazing intensity and grazing season on biodiversity in a large-scale field experiment.

• 
Developing and validating image-based indicators of vegetation structure and biodiversity condition from field and drone imagery.

• 
Contributing to the development of AI-based methods for mapping vegetation and habitat condition from drone images.

The project offers an opportunity to contribute to evidence-based conservation and the development of practical tools that can support land managers, farmers, conservation practitioners and value-chain actors in documenting biodiversity outcomes. The findings will help build a stronger scientific foundation for biodiversity-friendly grazing practices and nature-based beef production.

Qualifications and specific competences:

Applicants to the PhD position must have a Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in biology or equivalent. The applicants have documented experience in botanical surveys including species identification skills of North-European flora. The applicant must have a driver license applicable in Denmark. Demonstrated proficiency in data management and analysis, image analysis, and experience using R.

Place of employment and place of work:

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is C.F. Møllers Allé 8, building 1110, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contacts:

Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:

• Senior researcher, head of section Camilla Fløjgaard, e-mail: camf@ecos.au.dk (main supervisor)

For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:

Preferred starting date is 1 March 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:

Formalities and salary range

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

**Genmab is committed to transparency of clinical trial research. We recognize the scientific and ethical value of sharing clinical trial information in a non-biased and timely manner to benefit patients and other external stakeholders. The Clinical Trial Disclosure & Transparency (CTD&T) team resides within Clinical Trial Delivery, which hosts key functions for ensuring successful conduct and reporting of clinical trials.

We are now looking for a new Senior Manager to join our CTD&T team. The role offers a meaningful blend of operational and strategic tasks in a collaborative environment where quality, shared purpose, and cross-functional support are central to how we work.

In the role as Senior Manager of CTD&T, you will be executing against the global and national disclosure regulations and requirements across the entire Genmab portfolio. This role engages with internal and external stakeholders to ensure consistent and responsible disclosure and transparency practices. The position requires strong expertise in disclosure requirements and regulatory processes, coupled with strong organizational and communication skills, while maintaining a commitment to quality, integrity, and advancing Genmab’s mission.

• Manage, track, and maintain overall responsibility for the disclosure of clinical trial protocols and results on ClinicalTrials.gov, EU CTIS, and other applicable registries/platforms.

• Support and provide guidance on redaction activities.

• Ensure development of plain language results summaries.

• Stay updated on industry guidelines to ensure compliance.

• Support in updating SOPs, contribute to process improvements, and maintain adherence to established standards.

• Oversee vendor performance related to transparency deliverables.

• Liaise with clinical CROs to ensure consistent messaging across study registries.

Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

We're creating a new role at the top of our Engineering career ladder: Lead Architect. It's the senior end of our Technical Track — the rung above Tech Lead — and today it's a role we've deliberately left lightly defined, because we want the first person in it to help define it. You'll set Factbird's technical direction: architecture, tooling, and the multi-year technology bets that shape where the product goes next.

This is our most senior technical role, with no direct reports — your authority comes from judgment and track record, not the org chart. You'll work alongside our Tech Leads in Factbird's technical leadership group, partner closely with our Director of Engineering, and be the person other senior engineers go to when a decision is genuinely hard to reverse.

About the Role

As Lead Architect, you own Factbird's company-wide technical vision: the architecture our services run on, the tooling and standards our engineers use every day, and the multi-year technology strategy that ties it all together. You make — or sign off on — the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse architecture calls, and you're accountable for getting them right with the full context of where the business is headed, not just where the code is today.

You'll work across a team built on Rust, React, Node.js, and AWS, with AI-assisted development already a core part of how we ship. Some of what this role owns is already well-defined — reviewing RFCs, stewarding language and platform standards, setting the team's AI-tooling strategy. Some of it isn't yet: Factbird is still a growing company, and part of the job is helping us figure out what technical leadership at this level should look like as we scale.

You'll thrive here if you'd rather be trusted with genuinely hard calls than manage a team, and if you can hold both the technical detail and the commercial context — cost, risk, market direction — well enough to make a technology bet you can still defend a year later.

What you'll do

Architecture & technical strategy

• Own Factbird's multi-year technology strategy, and make the high-stakes architecture calls that are hard to reverse — with cost, risk, and business context factored in, not just engineering elegance

• Author and drive major RFCs from proposal through to an actual decision, and review the highest-risk architecture changes across the team

• Act as steward for our core languages and frameworks — setting standards, library choices, and the platform's overall shape

• Make build-vs-buy calls for new technical capabilities, and bring a clear point of view on emerging technologies worth adopting

• Define the observability, reliability, and security posture the platform is held to

Tooling & standards

• Set the team's technical tooling and platform standards, and keep them evolving as the stack and the company grow

• Define Factbird's strategy for AI-assisted development — which tools we adopt, how we balance velocity against code quality, security, and IP risk, and where we draw the line

• Shape engineering-wide quality philosophy and help set the technical bar used in hiring interviews

• Help define shared components and reference architecture that other engineers build on, rather than reinvent

• Give input into technical org design and team topology as Engineering scales

Technical leadership & mentorship

• Act as the trusted technical advisor to our Director of Engineering and the technical leadership group, partnering with Tech Leads and Product Leads on cross-team alignment

• Mentor senior engineers and Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without formal ownership of their people management

• Communicate technical vision and trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including leadership

• Identify technical risks to the business early, and say so before they become expensive

• Represent Factbird's technical thinking externally where it makes sense — a talk, a blog post, an open-source contribution — though this isn't a requirement on day one

What we’re looking for

We're looking for someone who's already earned this kind of trust somewhere else — someone whose technical opinions carry weight because they're right more often than not, and who'd rather solve the interesting, ambiguous problem than manage the team solving it.

The ideal background

• 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience, including real time spent as an architect or equivalent senior technical authority, not just a senior engineer with a bigger title

• A track record of owning multi-year technology strategy or platform architecture decisions that other teams had to live with — and that held up

• Has led major RFCs or architecture proposals cross-team, through genuine pushback, to an actual decision

• Comfortable making build-vs-buy and technology-adoption calls that account for cost, risk, and where the market is heading, not just what's technically interesting

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without needing formal authority to do it

• Practical, current experience with AI-assisted development, and a clear point of view on where it genuinely helps versus where it creates risk

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

We'd love to hear from you

If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Cristina Vartej at crva@factbird.com

Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027.

Title:
Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments

Research area and project description:
How can grazing management be optimized to benefit both biodiversity and nature-based beef production? This PhD project will address this question through analyses of long-term biodiversity monitoring data, development of digital biodiversity indicators, and field experiments in Danish semi-natural habitats.

Grazing is a key ecological process in many ecosystems. However, biodiversity outcomes depend on how grazing is managed, including grazing intensity and timing. Despite its widespread use as a conservation tool, important knowledge gaps remain regarding which grazing strategies deliver the greatest biodiversity benefits and how these outcomes can be documented in a robust and scalable way.

The PhD project is part of the interdisciplinary Nature&Beef initiative and will combine ecology, biodiversity monitoring, remote sensing and data science. The selected candidate will work with unique datasets from the Danish national biodiversity monitoring programme (NOVANA), field experiments, drone imagery and other digital monitoring approaches.

The project will focus on four interconnected themes:
1) Identifying grazing practices associated with positive biodiversity outcomes using long-term monitoring data.
2) Evaluating the effects of grazing intensity and grazing season on biodiversity in a large-scale field experiment.
3) Developing and validating image-based indicators of vegetation structure and biodiversity condition from field and drone imagery.
4) Contributing to the development of AI-based methods for mapping vegetation and habitat condition from drone images.

The project offers an opportunity to contribute to evidence-based conservation and the development of practical tools that can support land managers, farmers, conservation practitioners and value-chain actors in documenting biodiversity outcomes. The findings will help build a stronger scientific foundation for biodiversity-friendly grazing practices and nature-based beef production.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants to the PhD position must have a Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in biology or equivalent. The applicants have documented experience in botanical surveys including species identification skills of North-European flora. The applicant must have a driver license applicable in Denmark. Demonstrated proficiency in data management and analysis, image analysis, and experience using R.

jobs.description:
The Department of Communication and Arts at Roskilde University invites applications for one or two postdoctoral position(s) in a new research project on digital media and the conditions for democratic debate. The position is a full-time appointment for 24 months, starting on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

We welcome candidates with backgrounds in digital methods, computational social science, science and technology studies (STS), sociology, communication studies, political communication, media studies, information studies, digital humanities, or related fields in the humanities and social sciences.

About the project
The postdoc position is associated with an ambitious three-year project funded by the Politiken Foundation (Politiken-Fonden) through its largest ever research initiative, which seeks to investigate how digital technologies are shaping democratic debate. You will be part of a team researching how digital news media, search engines, social media, and AI chatbots present pressing issues in Danish public debate. Our central concern is the scope of public issues as they are represented online, how this varies between platforms and between people's actual online experiences, and how digital media shape the range of perspectives citizens encounter. While much research and public debate focuses on misinformation, disinformation, polarisation and hate speech, another fundamental question is whether digital media expose us to a sufficiently diverse range of actors, arguments, and viewpoints to support a productive democratic conversation. Do digital platforms broaden the range of concerns and perspectives that can enter democratic debate, or do they narrow the ways in which public issues are represented and understood?

The project will answer this by developing two complementary research tools:

• The Democratic Debate Meter: A public-facing digital tool that systematically tracks and compares how selected public issues — such as hybrid warfare, agricultural taxation, health services, or school reform — are represented across digital platforms. Using computational digital methods, including text analysis and simulated searches, we investigate which actors and topics become visible.
• The Live Data Donation Lab: A participatory research initiative that combines data donations with browser-based capture of digital content. Working with citizens, journalists, and policymakers, we investigate how personalised digital environments shape people's encounters with and sensemaking around public issues and involve participants in interpreting findings and developing our analytical approach.
By combining computational analysis with qualitative and participatory methods, the project aims to advance research on digital media and democracy. We are focused on producing publicly accessible findings, reports and tools that contribute to wider debates about the role of digital platforms in democratic life, while also contributing to cutting edge academic research at the highest international level.

The position
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will play a central role in the project's research activities, working closely with the project leaders and other team members. You will contribute to the collection and analysis of digital data, the development of methods for comparing representations of public issues across platforms, and the interpretation and communication of findings. Depending on your background and interests, there will be opportunities to contribute to computational text analysis, methodological development, public-facing data visualizations, qualitative research, participatory workshops and public dissemination. You will also contribute to the project's research publications and its public-facing outputs, including the Debate Meter and reports on the scope of issue representation across digital media.

The position offers an opportunity to develop an independent research profile while collaborating on a bold interdisciplinary project that connects methodological innovation with an important question for contemporary democracy. You will be part of an enthusiastic and supportive research environment at Roskilde University, with opportunities to participate in international conferences, workshops and research collaborations. In recent years, faculty have enjoyed a highly successful record of obtaining research grants for large national and international projects broadly focused on questions around digitalisation and democracy, meaning you will be joining a department where young and senior scholars are actively collaborating on a number of ambitious research initiatives in these areas.

The position is based at the Department of Communication and Arts, with affiliation to the Centre for Digital Citizenship and the Digital Media Lab. You will work closely with the project leader, Associate Professor Andreas Birkbak, and the co-investigator Professor Chris Peters.

Qualifications
We are looking for a researcher who is curious about how digital technologies shape public debate and who is interested in developing innovative ways to study these processes. Applicants must hold a PhD, or expect to obtain one by the time of appointment, in a relevant field within social science, the humanities, or data science.We are particularly interested in candidates who bring some combination of the following:

• Computational and digital methods: Experience with, or a strong interest in developing, computational approaches to digital data, especially text analysis and digital trace data and the comparative analysis of online content. Experience with qualitative, participatory or interpretive methods is also an advantage.
• Research on media and democracy: An interest in how digital media shape public debate, democratic participation and the visibility of different actors, issues and perspectives.
• Theoretical and methodological breadth: Familiarity with relevant approaches in STS, digital methods, media and communication studies, platform studies, controversy mapping, or related fields.
• Research communication: An interest in communicating research beyond academia, including through public reports, digital visualisations, workshops, or engagement with journalists and other societal actors.
• Good command of Danish is essential, as the project analyses Danish-language media content and public debate. Good command of English is also required, including the ability to write and publish research in English.
We do not expect candidates to be equally experienced in all these areas. We welcome applicants with complementary profiles who can contribute their own expertise while developing new skills through collaboration with the project team.

Responsibilities
The successful candidate(s) will be expected to:

• Contribute actively to the design and implementation of the project's research activities.
• Collect, process and analyse digital media data, including contributing to computational text analysis.
• Develop and apply analytical methods, in dialogue with the project's theoretical and empirical concerns.
• Contribute to research publications, both independently and in collaboration with the project team.
• Help communicate research to wider audiences through reports, digital outputs and other activities.
• Participate in workshops, conferences and collaborations with academic and non-academic partners.
• Contribute to the department's collegial and interdisciplinary research environment.
Assessment
In assessing applicants, particular consideration will be given to:

• The relevance and quality of the applicant's research experience and publications
• Potential for contributing to computational and digital methods and methodological innovation.
• The applicant's established theoretical and empirical interests on digital media and democracy.
• Experience with interdisciplinary collaboration and communicating research to wider audiences.
• Potential to contribute to the project and to the wider research environment at Roskilde University.
Further information
For further information about the position or the project, please contact the project leader Associate Professor Andreas Birkbak, at andreasbi@ruc.dk or +45 28 79 93 16. We expect job interviews to be held in February 2027.
